Heads up: the Google Ads conversion tag broke on Aug 7 after the site redeploy. Fixed on Aug 13. Conversions reported for that window are not real — don't read anything into them.
— Priya, Web

notes.text:
We 1.6x'd TikTok budget from the week of Aug 15 to test whether it scales. Agreed with finance that we'd evaluate after 6 weeks and cut if TikTok CPA is more than 1.5x Meta's CPA over the test period.
— Dan, Growth
notes.rule: cut if cpa(tiktok)/cpa(meta) > 1.5 over the test period

notes.text:
Brand awareness campaign went live on Meta the week of Sep 1. It's upper-funnel: expect spend to jump and last-click conversions to look worse for a while. Don't judge it on direct CPA.
— Maya, Brand

Q3 targets: blended CPA under $65, and weekly revenue above $25k by the end of September.
— Leadership

drafts:
## Headline
Blended spend increased in the latest week, but conversions and revenue declined, leading to a higher blended CPA that missed targets. Several channel-specific changes and data caveats require attention.

## Last week vs the period
Blended spend in week 12 was $23,030 [F1], 10.8% higher [F1] than the $20,785.27 [F1] weekly average over weeks 1-11. However, blended conversions in week 12 were 288 [F2], 1.7% lower [F2] than the 293 [F2] weekly average, and blended revenue in week 12 was $17,856 [F3], 1.7% lower [F3] than the $18,166 [F3] weekly average. Blended CPA in week 12 was $79.97 [F4], 12.7% higher [F4] than the $70.94 [F4] baseline.

## What the numbers mean
Google Search CPA in week 6 was $202.90 [F5], 222.1% higher [F5] than the $62.99 [F5] baseline, but this data is invalid [N1] due to a conversion tag break between Aug 7-13 [N1]. The weekly data cannot isolate the affected days. Email CPA in week 8 was $23.25 [F8], 35.7% higher [F8] than the $17.14 [F8] baseline.

TikTok spend averaged $4,787.83 per week [F6] over weeks 7-12, 66.7% higher [F6] than the $2,872.33 [F6] weekly average baseline, as part of an experiment to scale budget [N2]. The ratio of TikTok CPA to Meta CPA over weeks 7-12 was 1.92x [F11]. The agreed evaluation rule [N2] is to cut TikTok if its CPA is more than 1.5x [N2] Meta's CPA over the test period.

Meta spend averaged $8,935.50 per week [F7] over weeks 9-12, 26.9% higher [F7] than the $7,040.38 [F7] weekly average baseline, due to a brand awareness campaign launch [N3] the week of Sep 1 [N3]. This campaign is upper-funnel and should not be judged on direct CPA [N3].

Blended CPA in week 12 was $79.97 [F9], which did not meet the Q3 target of under $65 [N4]. Blended revenue in week 12 was $17,856 [F10], which did not meet the Q3 target of above $25k [N4]. The Q3 target period is incomplete [N4], as data ends Sep 28 but targets are due Sep 30 [N4].

## Decisions needed
Evaluate the TikTok experiment based on the CPA ratio against Meta.

## Recommended actions
- Review TikTok performance against the 1.5x [N2] Meta CPA threshold for the test period.
- Investigate the Email CPA outlier in week 8 [F8] for potential causes or lasting impact.
- Monitor blended CPA and revenue closely for the remainder of Q3 to assess target attainment.

## Data caveats
Google Ads conversion data for Google Search between Aug 7-13 [N1] (week 6) is invalid [N1], affecting CPA for that period. The Q3 target period for blended CPA and revenue is incomplete [N4], with data ending Sep 28 [N4] and targets due Sep 30 [N4].
